> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **5** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c7dcb451928dfad914a869fdb86909459b63a3a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 9b79d6a504ed8bc283a82debac5c9bb2684f0bc1 && git checkout 9b79d6a504ed8bc283a82debac5c9bb2684f0bc1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4c7dcb451928dfad914a869fdb86909459b63a3a f827e706365a462b6a3688149e5ceec197d11b78 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4c7dcb451928dfad914a869fdb86909459b63a3a && git merge --no-ff f827e706365a462b6a3688149e5ceec197d11b78

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c7dcb451928dfad914a869fdb86909459b63a3a
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f827e706365a462b6a3688149e5ceec197d11b78`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-ui.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-setup-access.pin.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-platform-managed.pin.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-auth-gate.pin.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/error-envelope.conformance.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/connection-credential-store.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-runtime-version.pin.test.ts + packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/setup.app.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-route-ledger.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/index.ts, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs, .changeset/25097-cloud-connection-platform-managed.md (each rewritten sentence judged below, at the seat's order), .changeset/25119-cloud-connection-one-rule.md (the level, ②). The face is narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and on the changeset), so the floor is every path outside the prose faces; `content/docs/deployment/cloud-connection.mdx` and the changeset prose are the lane seat's ACCEPT. Inputs: card #25119 (body and four comments), card #25113 (body and two comments), PR #25143 (body, 12-file list, net diff against `main` at the base `abc25a3536`, which is the merge-base with current `origin/main`), and the 49 check-runs on this head. Line numbers below are the head's, read with `git show` by sha.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) One reading of the grant — RIGHT.** `holdsPlatformSettings` (`cloud-connection-plugin.ts:532-564`) is the only reader of the capability on this surface. It hands the session already read to `resolveAuthzContext` (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:468`), counts the answer only when `authz.credential === 'session'` and `authz.userId === caller.userId` (`:558`, so a key riding beside a session lends nothing), and reads `systemPermissions` for `CLOUD_CONNECTION_CAPABILITY` (`:559`), the one constant `'manage_platform_settings'` declared at `cloud-connection-ui.ts:35` and imported at `:149`. Its four call sites are `:605` (the `status` full-record branch), `:690` (`bind/start`), `:754` (`bind/poll`) and `:862` (`unbind`); no `setup.access` or `SETUP_ACCESS` literal survives in the plugin outside the header prose (`:66`). The literal and the refusal shape are the #9593 precedent's: `DATASOURCE_ADMIN_CAPABILITY = 'manage_platform_settings'` (`service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts:283`) refused as `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` with a message naming the capability (`:570-576`); `CAPABILITY_REFUSAL` (`cloud-connection-plugin.ts:171-175`) is the same status and code. The other four routes of this plugin — `install` (`:906-950`), `installation` (`:957-1011`), `installed` (`:1019-1054`), `org-packages` (`:1062-1095`) — take any signed-in session, as at the base, and the diff does not touch them; none changes the connection and none serves `environmentId` or `connection` (`installed` and `org-packages` serve `connected: Boolean(credential())`, which is the `bound` every caller already gets from `status`). So no door, no branch and no other route of this plugin admits a `setup.access`-only caller to what ruling 乙 gates. The narrow `status` shape is exactly `{ bound, runtimeId, provider }` (`:610`), byte-equal to the base's; the full record is served only past `caller && !caller.authGate && holdsPlatformSettings` (`:605`), and a permission-store outage withholds it (`:606-609`). Nothing leaks more.

**(b) Widening — none that the ruling did not order.** Before: the three doors and the full record admitted a session holding `setup.access`. After: one holding `manage_platform_settings`. Under the shipped sets this is a strict narrowing — `organization_admin` carries `['manage_org_users', 'setup.access', 'setup.write', 'manage_mailboxes']` (`default-permission-sets.ts:418`) and loses every door and the full record; `admin_full_access` carries `manage_platform_settings` (the datasource gate's own docblock, `admin-routes.ts:274-276`) and keeps them. One edge is named for the seat: a hand-authored set holding `manage_platform_settings` WITHOUT `setup.access` (the pin's `platform_operator`) was refused at the base and is served now. That is the replacement ruling 乙 ordered ("replaces `setup.access`", card body) and the shape the #9593 doors already take for the same capability, so it is the diff doing what was ruled, not a defect; the claim's "Nothing widens" reads as qualified by it. On a managed runtime `bind/start` and `bind/poll` move from served to refused — narrowing. The `403` keeps its status and code and now names `manage_platform_settings`; the `409` keeps its status, code and first sentence (`:199-204`). The package's public export set is unchanged: `index.ts:81` exports `CloudConnectionSettingsPage` and `CLOUD_CONNECTION_UI_BUNDLE` at the base and at the head, and `CLOUD_CONNECTION_CAPABILITY` is not re-exported from the barrel; the bundle's value gains `requiredPermissions` on one item (additive).

**(c) Managed runtime: 409 after identity and capability, before any control-plane call or store write — RIGHT at all three doors.** `platformManaged` is `cloudApiKey !== ''`, resolved once at `kernel:ready` (`:316`, `:335`), the same fact `credential()` reads (`:342`). Traced line by line:
- `bind/start` (`:668-731`): body parse `:671` (a malformed body is `400` first, the base's position) → `resolveEnvironmentId` `:678` (reads the store or the local env registry; no write, no cloud) → `resolveSession` `:685` → held session `403` `:686` → `401` `:687` → capability `403` `:690` → **`platformManaged` → `refusePlatformManaged` `:693`** → `CLOUD_UNCONFIGURED` `:694` → first `fetch` `:696`. This handler writes the store nowhere.
- `bind/poll` (`:737-846`): body `:740` → env `:743` → session `:750` → gate `:751` → `401` `:752` → capability `:754` → **managed `409` `:759`** → `cloudUrl` `:760` → `device_code` `400` `:763` → token `fetch` `:766` → `/bind` `fetch` `:807` → `store.write` `:827`.
- `unbind` (`:853-899`): env `:854` → session `:858` → gate `:859` → `401` `:860` → capability `:862` → **managed `409` `:866`** → revoke `fetch` `:875` → `store.write`/`clear` `:892`/`:895`. The base's inline `409` is replaced by the shared `refusePlatformManaged` (`:577-578`) with the same status and code at the same position.
One constant (`PLATFORM_MANAGED_REFUSAL`, `:199-204`) and one helper serve the three. The `409` precedes the `CLOUD_UNCONFIGURED` `503` on every door, as `unbind` already did at the base.

**(d) The page is ungatable by key; the nav item's key is live — RIGHT.** `PageSchema` is a `lazySchema` over a `strictObject` at `packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts:1868`; its shape declares no `requiredPermissions` (the file's only two occurrences, `:164` and `:769`, are inside component-prop descriptions), and its guidance refuses `permissions` with "a page is not permission-gated by a field — gate the DATA it shows with the object's permission sets" (`:1932`). So H2 is correctly disproven, and `packages/spec/**` (out of scope) stays untouched. The server's nav filter is `filterAppForUserWithReason` (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:974`): `filterNav` applies `holdsRequiredPermissions(e.requiredPermissions, sysPerms)` to every entry, groups included (`:1018`), and recurses into `children` (`:1102-1105`); it is called from the `/meta` app reads at `:1173`, `:1639` and `:1863`, which `app.zod.ts:1265-1270` states ("enforced server-side in both trees"). So `requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']` on `nav_cloud_connection` (`cloud-connection-ui.ts:112`) is read by the server, not inert; today it is redundant with `group_integrations`' own gate (`setup.app.ts:108`), and it is the shape `nav_datasources` takes in the same group (`datasource-admin-plugin.ts:577-583`). The managed pin asserts the key on the merged tree the protocol service serves (upstream of that filter), and the setup-access pin asserts it on the bundle with the literal spelled in the test, not the constant.

**(e) Pins — updated, nothing loosened.** `expectCapabilityRefusal` (setup-access pin) asserts `403`, `code === 'PERMISSION_DENIED'`, `BaseResponseSchema`, `envelopeViolations`, `ApiErrorSchema`, a message naming `manage_platform_settings` AND not naming `setup.access` — one assertion more than the base's helper — for every door × two unpermitted callers (a member, and the `organization_admin` default set) × both connection shapes × both modes, each with zero control-plane calls and the stored token untouched. `expectManagedRefusal` asserts status and `code` (what the base's managed control asserted) with zero calls and the token untouched; the managed `409`'s full envelope is held in the platform-managed pin per door × both modes (status, code, `BaseResponseSchema`, `envelopeViolations`, `ApiErrorSchema`, message prefix, zero calls, stored record neither replaced nor cleared) and in `error-envelope.conformance` per door (`expectDeclaredErrorEnvelope` status + code). The auth-gate pin's managed UN-HELD case asserts `409`, `code` and no call for each of the three doors. `status`: both non-holders now get the EXACT narrow object (tighter than the base's sorted-keys check); both holders (`admin_full_access`, and an org-scoped `platform_operator`) get the exact full record; the key-beside-session cases run for both non-holders at `bind/start` and at `status`. The one base assertion gone is the managed CONTROL that served `bind/start` and `bind/poll` `200` on a managed runtime — the behaviour this PR removes, now pinned as `409`. The three fixtures whose subject is not the permission grant the admin `manage_platform_settings` beside `setup.access` and change nothing else. H5 holds as stated: the route ledger's four binding rows (`cloud-connection-route-ledger.ts:109-150`) carry a disposition and a note and name no gate.

**The pending `.changeset/25097-cloud-connection-platform-managed.md`, sentence by sentence (the seat's landing rule for the `check-empty-changeset` deliberate-correction red).** Before = `origin/main` at the base; after = this head. Each judged against the head's behaviour with the deciding line.

1. Paragraph 3, second sentence. BEFORE: "A request to disconnect it is refused with `409` and `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, after the sign-in and Setup Access checks and before anything is revoked or cleared." — FALSE of the head: the check before the `409` reads `manage_platform_settings`, not Setup Access (`cloud-connection-plugin.ts:862`). AFTER: "... after the sign-in and capability checks and before anything is revoked or cleared." — TRUE: session `:858`, auth gate `:859`, `401` `:860`, capability `:862`, `409` `:866`, revoke `:875`, clear `:892`/`:895`.
2. Paragraph 4, last sentence. BEFORE: "The connect and disconnect requests still take Setup Access alone." — FALSE of the head: `:690`, `:754`, `:862` read `manage_platform_settings`, and the `organization_admin` set (`default-permission-sets.ts:418`), which holds Setup Access, is refused (setup-access pin, every door). AFTER: the sentence is dropped — RIGHT; what remains of the paragraph is judged under 6-8 below.
3. The BREAKING list's "Unchanged" bullet. BEFORE: "a runtime without the service key, apart from the entry's group. The connection status answer is unchanged on every runtime." — FALSE of the head on both sentences: the permission the doors read moved (`:690`, `:754`, `:862`), and who is served the full status record moved with it (`:605`). AFTER: "a runtime without the service key, apart from the entry's group and the permission its connect and disconnect requests and its connection details require, which another change in this release raises to `manage_platform_settings`. The connection status answer is otherwise unchanged on every runtime." — TRUE: the permission is the one at `:690`/`:754`/`:862`/`:605`; the two status shapes are unchanged (`:598-611`), only the line between them moved, which "otherwise" carries; "another change in this release" is the 25119 note beside it. Wording note, non-blocking: "raises to" can be read as "adds on top of"; the head REPLACES `setup.access` with `manage_platform_settings` (edge in (b)); the 25119 note states the replacement precisely.
4. Frontmatter `'@objectstack/cloud-connection': minor` — untouched; a foreign entry graded on its own PR, not re-graded here (the level axis judges the entries a PR introduces, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs:7-16`).
5. Title line ("... registers no Cloud Connection Setup page and refuses to disconnect; everywhere else the Cloud Connection entry moves to Setup's Integrations group") — TRUE: no registration when managed `:412-423`; `unbind` refused `:866`; `group_integrations` at `cloud-connection-ui.ts:103`. The head refuses connect too; the sentence states less than the head does, nothing false.
6. Paragraph 2 (the defect as it was: the page in the Apps group reading "Connected", the disconnect clearing the device credential while the key stayed in use) — history in the past tense, TRUE as history; not a claim about the head's behaviour.
7. Paragraph 3, first and third sentences: "Such a runtime now registers neither the page nor its navigation entry, and says so once at boot." — TRUE: `:412-417` (one `info` line), `:418-423` (registration only when not managed); the managed pin's "says so once at boot" case holds it. "The message says the platform manages the connection." — TRUE: `PLATFORM_MANAGED_REFUSAL` (`:199-204`) opens "This runtime's cloud connection is managed by the platform".
8. Paragraph 4, remaining sentences: "A self-hosted or local runtime, connected through the device-code flow, keeps the page and its disconnect unchanged." — TRUE in the sentence's own contrast with the managed runtime, which loses both: the page registers (`:418-423`) and `unbind` still revokes and clears (`:868-898`). Read alone, "its disconnect unchanged" could be taken as "who may disconnect is unchanged", which this release changes; the amended Unchanged bullet (3) carries that qualification in the same note, and the 25119 note states it. Non-blocking; the seat may tighten it to "keeps the page and can still disconnect" if it wants no reading left open. "Its Cloud Connection entry moves from the Apps group to the Integrations group, after Webhooks, Datasources and Connect an Agent." — TRUE: priority 200 (`cloud-connection-ui.ts:104`) against 100 (`webhook-outbox-plugin.ts:256`), 100 (`datasource-admin-plugin.ts:574`) and 110 (`mcp/src/connect-ui.ts:104`). "That group requires `manage_platform_settings`, so a user who holds Setup Access without it, such as an organization administrator, no longer sees the entry." — TRUE: `setup.app.ts:108`; `filterNav` drops the group for a caller lacking it (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:1018`); `default-permission-sets.ts:418`.
9. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — the note's own declaration of its own change; unchanged and still true of it.
10. The adr-0087 marker comment ("not-required (no-migration-prescription) ... no exported declaration is removed or narrowed ... The navigation entry's new group is a value inside an exported constant whose type is unchanged ...") — TRUE: `index.ts:81` is the same at base and head; the group is a value in `CLOUD_CONNECTION_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS` (`cloud-connection-ui.ts:100-116`).
11. The BREAKING banner ("on a runtime holding the environment service key, a disconnect request it carried out is now refused, and the Cloud Connection page and its navigation entry are no longer served"), "shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention" — TRUE of the head (`:866`, `:412-423`) and of its own frontmatter; the convention phrase predates ruling A and belongs to that note's own PR.
12. "Nothing to rewrite: ... A self-hosted server leaves `OS_CLOUD_API_KEY` unset ...; one that sets it is platform-managed by this rule." — TRUE: `:316`, `:335`.

Verdict on the rewrite: each of the three changes replaces a sentence FALSE of this head with one TRUE of it, or drops it; every untouched sentence is true of this head. This record is the written confirmation `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs:541-563` asks for (`FOREIGN_CORRECTION_REMEDY`: do NOT restore it; say so on the PR and get it confirmed), beside the PR body's Acceptance-notes bullet.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25119-cloud-connection-one-rule.md`: `'@objectstack/cloud-connection': patch`; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: none`; a **BREAKING** banner naming who loses what; an adr-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; and the migration in the body ("Who acts: ... grants `manage_platform_settings` ... through a permission set or a position"). The PR body carries the same two declaration lines at line start. Judged right: `Metadata-protocol: none` because nothing an author can write moves — `PageSchema` is untouched, `packages/spec/**` is not in the file list, and `requiredPermissions` on a navigation item is an already-authorable key (`app.zod.ts:426`) whose VALUE on one shipped item changes. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3 ("`none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition") and the gate's rule (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs:7-16`, `:93-100`, ruling A on #25105), the level is `patch`; the card's "`minor` with the BREAKING banner" predates that rule, and the dev's deviation 1 names the conflict rather than following the card silently — correct. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right arm: a published accept set narrows (the `organization_admin` default set loses the three doors and the full record; a managed runtime loses two more doors), with the one replacement edge named in ①(b). The 25097 note's own frontmatter (`minor`) is foreign to this PR and untouched. Gate readings on this head: `Check Changeset` step 13 (ADR-0087 disposition) success and step 15 (major/level guard) success in both runs; its step 12 is red on `.changeset/25097-cloud-connection-platform-managed.md` with the foreign-changeset annotation (deliberate-correction class) — discharged above; `Check Changeset` is not one of the five required contexts.

Check-runs on this head, read as the gate verdicts: the five required contexts are all `success` — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (and 6/6 shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Every other run is `success` or `skipped` except `Check Changeset` (`failure`, two runs, step 12 only). `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` is `success` on this head (both runs). 12 files, +551/−324, under the 3,000-line human-merge threshold; no governed surface in the file list; head repo is the base repo.

### ③ Boundary flags
